subject.title: fix(cron): preserve edited schedules and simplify run ownership

question: Is the supplied automated coverage, together with a redacted real cron-service run showing an in-flight schedule edit survives completion, sufficient to land this compatibility-sensitive state change?
rationale: The patch changes persisted schedule-result semantics and the PR body summarizes tests rather than providing an inspectable after-fix runtime transcript; the protected maintainer label requires explicit human handling.

options.title: Require runtime transcript
options.body: Request a redacted terminal capture or runtime logs that edit a running job and show the stored next-run and force-marker results after both firing and quiet completion.

options.title: Accept automated evidence
options.body: Land based on the focused regression matrix and successful checks if the maintainers consider the cron test harness representative of the production persistence path.

options.title: Pause for a narrower proof
options.body: Hold the PR until the contributor can demonstrate the exact operator-edit race against the real cron service.

recommendation.title: Require runtime transcript
recommendation.body: Request a redacted terminal capture or runtime logs that edit a running job and show the stored next-run and force-marker results after both firing and quiet completion.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor authored the affected cron ownership and regression work and can most directly supply the requested behavior evidence.
